Primary_Lighting_Directive.Read_First: This directive is read BEFORE every preservation rule below and wins over all of them on the single question of lighting.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Core: The main light is being MOVED. The single most important result is that the SUBJECT'S OWN BODY must be visibly re-lit: the side of the face and body facing the light is directly lit by the new key light while the opposite side, turned away from it, falls into natural shadow, with a clear light-to-shadow boundary (terminator) running vertically across the face and body. If the subject still looks evenly/flatly lit like the original, the edit has FAILED, even if everything else is perfect.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Meaning_Of_Preserve: Every 'preserve / keep / do not change / unchanged' rule below protects SHAPE, GEOMETRY, ANATOMY, COLOR and TEXTURE ONLY. None of them protect the original brightness, the original flat lighting, or the original shadow pattern. Re-lighting the subject is REQUIRED, not optional.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Two_Carriers: Show the new direction on BOTH (1) cast shadows on whatever real surface exists, AND (2) form shading on the subject's own volume. If no surface exists to catch a cast shadow, carrier (2) alone must clearly prove the light direction.

Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, modify only the existing lighting and shadow structure of the image, never the content. Apply Original_Image_Preservation_Block, Subject_Preservation_Rule, Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule, Side_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control, Lighting_Effect_Block, Advanced_Light_Direction_Control, Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule, Light_Intensity_Control, Environment_Lighting_Control, Light_Color_Control, Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule, and Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule. When Switch is off, ignore this entire block.

Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Rule: Keep original image structure, aspect ratio, canvas size, framing, camera angle, perspective, crop boundary, subject scale and position, background layout, object placement, geometry, silhouettes, contours, spatial/depth/overlap relationships, color identity, material/skin/hair/fabric/background texture, surface detail, grain, noise and overall composition. The subject, background, props, clothing, accessories, body parts, hair, facial features and object/background contours must not be moved, resized, duplicated, removed, replaced, redrawn, warped, rotated, cropped, reframed, zoomed, reshaped, recolored or recomposed. Only lighting attributes — shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction/intensity, side-light modeling, shadow softness/density, cast-shadow behavior and environmental brightness — may be adjusted. Lighting may change perceived brightness and contrast but must not regenerate content.
Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Negative_Rule: No stretching, squeezing, warping, liquify, reshaping, slimming, enlarging, rotating, tilting, added canvas area, face/body reconstruction, pose/hand correction, perspective correction, auto-crop, zoom, reframing, object/background replacement, added/removed objects, style reinterpretation, or retouching beyond lighting-related highlight and shadow changes.

Subject_Preservation_Rule.Applicability: Applies to any identity-bearing living subject (person, character, animal, creature). For products, objects, architecture, interiors, landscapes, vehicles, food or still life, do not force face/eye/anatomy/skin/clothing rules; instead preserve their shape, proportions, material, text, logos, labels, structure, layout, surface detail, seams and edges. For scenes preserve terrain, sky, water, plants, roads, atmosphere, background structure and natural depth. Do not force person-specific lighting details onto non-person scenes.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Preserve: Keep the exact original identity and recognizability (same person/animal/character; same age, gender presentation, ethnicity cues, personality, character design); same face shape, facial proportions and anatomy — brows, eyes, nose, mouth, lips, teeth, jawline, chin, cheekbones, wrinkles, pores, freckles, scars, moles, makeup, facial hair, skin texture and expression; same body shape, proportions, head-to-body ratio, neck, shoulders, torso, limbs, hands, fingers, feet, posture, gesture, pose and silhouette; same hairstyle, length, volume, hairline, direction, texture and color; same clothing design, fit, folds, color, fabric, logos, patterns, accessories, jewelry, glasses, hats, bags, props and object interactions; same subject scale, position, crop boundary, framing, orientation, contact points and subject-to-background relationship. This rule fixes geometry, color and texture only — it does NOT fix brightness, lighting or shadow.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Eye_Gaze: If eyes are present, strictly preserve the original eye gaze, eye direction, line of sight, pupil and iris position, eyelid shape and openness, eye expression, catchlight position and emotional intent; do not make the subject look at the camera if they were not, or look away if they were, and do not change eye focus, eye contact, squinting or blinking state. Lighting may change highlights and shadows around the eyes only. If no eyes are present, ignore this and preserve the actual visible content.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Allowed_Changes: Only lighting attributes change: shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction and intensity, side-light brightness and hardness, shadow density and softness, cast-shadow behavior. Per Primary_Lighting_Directive the face, skin and body MUST be visibly re-lit and gain new directional shadows; identity, anatomy, texture and color stay the same.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Negative_Rule: No identity/face/expression/gaze/pose change; no body shape or proportion change; no hairstyle or hair-color change; no clothing or accessory change; no hand/finger/anatomy correction; no beautification, skin smoothing, airbrushing, slimming, aging, de-aging, stylization, realism reinterpretation, character redesign or person replacement; no retouching beyond lighting-related highlight and shadow changes.

Lighting_Control.Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule: Apply the selected left horizontal 0-degree side light to all visible subjects, objects and environment surfaces according to their actual geometry. Left-facing surfaces receive the light directly; right-facing and occluded surfaces, turned away from the light, fall into natural shadow; vertical planes, object sides, furniture, architecture, vehicles, foliage, terrain, fabric folds, cavities, recesses, edges and corners follow the same left-to-right light direction, shadow direction, falloff and material response. Preserve all original shapes, materials, textures, colors, proportions and spatial relationships. Material response is always governed by the surface's optical type, independent of light direction: opaque solids (stone, metal, wood, plastic, dense fabric) block the light into hard-edged highlights and shadow boundaries, with sharp speculars on metal/glossy/wet surfaces and diffuse falloff on matte ones; translucent or thin materials (glass, sheer gauze, thin fabric, leaves, petals, ears, skin and hair edges) transmit and scatter it, glowing with soft subsurface bleed and luminous edge transmission instead of a hard opaque edge. Apply the matching behavior to whatever material is present, preserving original color and texture.

Side_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Goal: Make the left horizontal side light reusable across people, products, objects, architecture, interiors, landscapes and full scenes by following visible surface orientation and spatial geometry rather than only human body parts.
Side_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Surface_Rule: The side light creates clear lateral modeling: surfaces facing the left light receive it directly, surfaces turned away fall into shadow, and forms gain visible side-to-side volume. It can model human faces/bodies, animal forms, product side planes, object bevels, furniture sides, architectural planes, vehicle panels, foliage masses, terrain forms, fabric folds, props, walls and floor objects.
Side_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Shadow_Rule: Cast and form shadows extend mainly away from the left-side light toward the right, consistent with a pure horizontal side light at subject/scene mid-height. Avoid diagonal top-down, bottom-up, frontal or backlit shadow logic.
Side_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Negative_Rule: No fake rim light, no backlight interpretation, no top-light interpretation, no frontal flash, no flat illumination, no object cutout look, no new edges, no altered silhouettes, no recolored materials, no changed geometry.

Lighting_Control.Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule: If the background is pure white, near-white, overexposed, or too bright for subject/object separation or side-light readability, the side light acting on the background carrier means reducing only the background luminance/value enough to create clear separation between the visible subject/foreground/scene contour and the background. This is part of re-lighting (the light reaching the background carrier), not a separate effect. Preserve original hue, color identity, saturation relationship, material/photographic texture, background objects, structure and composition. Do not recolor the background, add color cast or colored light, change geometry, add new objects, or change the subject/scene. The adjustment must behave like exposure/value reduction only, not color grading, and must support side-light readability without overriding the selected side horizontal light direction.
Lighting_Control.Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule: Do not create any visible light spots, patches, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flares, glow blobs, artificial halos, bright stains, colored light marks, caustic patterns, bokeh spots, decorative illumination or visible lamp effects on the background. The background may only receive realistic overall brightness, exposure, contrast and natural shadow changes caused by the selected key light direction. Preserve original background texture, color identity, surface material, object structure and composition. Do not add new light shapes or illumination patterns on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture, objects or any background surface.
Lighting_Control.Lighting_Effect_Block: Modify the existing lighting and shadow pattern only; replace the original illumination with a strong horizontal side light from the left side of the subject/object/scene at 0-degree vertical elevation. Preserve subject identity (if people/animals present), facial features, expression, eye gaze, skin/fur texture, body structure, pose, clothing, accessories, props, product shape, text, logos, architecture, furniture, landscape elements, background, composition, original color palette and material/photographic/overall image texture. Create clear side-light modeling: left-facing surfaces directly lit; right-facing and occluded surfaces turned away from the light and falling into natural shadow; more three-dimensional volume through lateral light and shadow, applied to faces, bodies, animal forms, product side planes, furniture, architecture, vehicles, foliage, terrain, water, folds and recesses. Photorealistic, pure lighting adjustment only: no fog, haze, extra objects, geometry/subject/face/eye-gaze/pose/clothing change, product or architecture redesign, scene-layout change, recoloring, color cast, background light spots, projected patches, spotlight circles, lens flare, glow blobs, or artificial halos.

Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Rule: Treat the main subject/object/scene center as the center of an imaginary sphere. The light source is positioned on that sphere and always points toward the visible content. For this mode, use only the selected side horizontal lighting direction at 0-degree vertical elevation. Do not reinterpret it as top, upper-side, front, back, bottom, rim, or diagonal portrait light. Express the selected side 0-degree position through visible highlight placement, opposite-side shadow density, cast shadow direction, surface-facing illumination and environmental lighting consistency. Do not alter the original subject/object/scene geometry, composition, text, logos or material identity while changing the lighting direction.
Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Ignore_Unselected_Rule: Horizontal_Position_Options and Vertical_Position_Options are a reference menu only. Apply ONLY the option named in Selected_Horizontal_Position / Selected_Vertical_Position. All other options are inactive references and must NOT influence the lighting direction, highlights, shadows or cast shadow behavior.
Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Active_Direction_Prompt: main light source positioned directly to the left side of the subject, object or scene on the horizontal plane at 0-degree vertical elevation, about 90 degrees from the camera-facing direction. This is a pure side horizontal light, not top, not upper-side, not front, not back, not bottom, not rim light. The light rays travel horizontally from left to right toward the visible content. Left-facing surfaces receive the strongest illumination — human left facial/body planes, animal left-side planes, product side planes, object bevels, furniture sides, architecture planes, vehicles, foliage, terrain, water, props, folds and other left-facing surfaces. Right-facing surfaces are turned away from the light and fall into natural shadow, creating strong lateral modeling and a clear three-dimensional side-light structure. Cast shadows extend mainly toward the right side. Avoid frontal key, top, upper-left, back, bottom-up, colored and rim light. Preserve the exact original image content, person identity and gaze if present, product shape, text, logos, object geometry, architecture, scene layout, pose, clothing, body structure and character design if present.

Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Override_Note: OVERRIDES the lighting implied by every preservation rule above: those rules protect SHAPE, GEOMETRY, COLOR and TEXTURE only, never the original brightness, flat/even lighting or shadow pattern. The subject's face, skin and body MUST be re-lit and MUST visibly gain new shadows from the selected direction, while identity, anatomy and texture stay unchanged.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Rule: Because the main light is being changed, the new directional key light MUST produce a clearly visible lighting change on TWO carriers at the same time, in every image regardless of scene type: (1) CAST SHADOWS on any shadow-receiving surface actually present (ground, floor, walls, nearby objects) following the selected direction; and (2) FORM SHADING directly on the subject's own face, skin, body and volume. Both carriers are required together; never rely on cast shadows alone and never rely on subject shading alone. Carrier (2) is mandatory for floating, isolated or background-less subjects, where it is the ONLY way to read the light direction. For carrier (2): the left-facing planes of the face (left cheek, forehead, jaw, left side of the nose), neck, arms, hands, torso, legs, clothing and every 3D surface detail (knit ribs, raised bobbles, fabric folds, seams, accessories, product bevels, object faces) receive the new key light directly, while the right-facing planes are turned away from it and receive only ambient fill, falling into natural shadow and producing a visible vertical terminator (a continuous light-to-shadow boundary) down the face and body. Use cylindrical or rounded forms (head, arms, torso, bobbles, limbs) as clear left-lit / right-shadowed volume cues. The key light reaches the left-facing planes and not the right-facing planes, so the left-to-right contrast follows naturally; do not artificially darken or brighten either side — render the real physical result. The result must look clearly relit and different from the original in light and shadow, while remaining the exact same subject, geometry, color, texture and composition.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Surface_Absence_Rule: If a shadow-receiving surface is genuinely absent or too far to catch a realistic cast shadow (e.g. subject against open sky, a seamless backdrop or a gradient), do not fabricate fake ground or background shadows; in that case carrier (2) subject form shading alone must carry the full, strong directional effect on the face and body. When a valid surface IS present, both carriers must show the change together.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Negative_Rule: Do not output flat, even, frontal, ambient or original-style uniform lighting on the subject; do not keep the face and body evenly lit; do not leave both sides equally bright; do not let the subject look unchanged from the original; do not treat 'preserve identity/skin/face' as a reason to skip relighting the subject; do not issue brightness-operation instructions such as 'darken / dim / brighten / lift / reduce fill on one side' — describe only the physics (key light from the left, the opposite side turned away and lit by ambient fill) and let the shading be the natural result; do not add fake background shadows on sky or seamless backdrops; do not express the direction on only one carrier.

Horizontal_Position_Options.front: light source positioned directly in front of the subject on the horizontal plane, aligned with the camera-facing direction. The rays travel from front to back. Front-facing surfaces receive soft even illumination, rear-facing surfaces fall only slightly into shadow, cast shadows extend minimally behind. Clean frontal lighting with minimal left-right bias.
Horizontal_Position_Options.front_right: light source at the front-right of the subject on the horizontal plane, about 45 degrees from front. The rays travel diagonally from front-right. Front-right surfaces receive the strongest illumination, left and rear surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the back-left. Three-quarter frontal lighting with right-side modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.right: light source directly to the right of the subject on the horizontal plane, about 90 degrees from front. The rays travel horizontally from right to left. Right-facing surfaces receive the strongest illumination, left-facing surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the left. Strong right-side lighting with clear lateral modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back_right: light source at the back-right of the subject on the horizontal plane, about 135 degrees from front. The rays travel diagonally from back-right. Back-right surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-left surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the front-left. Rear three-quarter lighting with edge separation and partial silhouette.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back: light source positioned directly behind the subject on the horizontal plane at 0-degree vertical elevation, opposite the camera-facing direction. The rays travel horizontally from back to front toward the camera. Back-facing surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-facing surfaces no longer receive the key light and read naturally as the side turned away from it, cast shadows extend toward the camera/front. Pure horizontal backlighting with strong silhouette structure.
Horizontal_Position_Options.back_left: light source at the back-left of the subject on the horizontal plane, about 135 degrees from front on the left. The rays travel diagonally from back-left. Back-left surfaces and outer contours receive the strongest illumination, front-right surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the front-right. Rear three-quarter lighting with edge separation and partial silhouette.
Horizontal_Position_Options.left: light source directly to the left of the subject on the horizontal plane at 0-degree elevation, about 90 degrees from front. The rays travel horizontally from left to right. Left-facing surfaces receive the strongest illumination, right-facing surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the right. Pure horizontal side lighting with clear lateral modeling.
Horizontal_Position_Options.front_left: light source at the front-left of the subject on the horizontal plane, about 45 degrees from front. The rays travel diagonally from front-left. Front-left surfaces receive the strongest illumination, right and rear surfaces fall into shadow, cast shadows extend toward the back-right. Three-quarter frontal lighting with left-side modeling.

Vertical_Position_Options.top_90: light source directly above the subject at +90 degrees elevation, pure zenith, beam aimed vertically downward. Strongest highlights on upward-facing surfaces, top planes and upper edges; side surfaces darker; undersides, recesses and lower planes fall into deep shadow. Cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath. Ignore horizontal direction.
Vertical_Position_Options.upper_45: light source above the subject at about +45 degrees elevation, between horizontal and top, beam aimed diagonally downward. Upper planes and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive highlights; lower planes, undersides and opposite-facing surfaces fall into controlled shadow. Cast shadows travel diagonally downward and away.
Vertical_Position_Options.horizontal_0: light source positioned at 0 degrees elevation on the horizontal plane around the subject, at approximately mid-height. The rays travel horizontally, parallel to the ground, striking the subject from the selected horizontal position at the same vertical height, not from above or below. Surfaces facing the light are illuminated, opposite-facing surfaces fall into shadow, while top- and bottom-facing planes receive little direct light. Cast shadows extend mainly horizontally away from the selected direction. Avoid overhead and bottom-up lighting.
Vertical_Position_Options.lower_45: light source positioned below the subject at about -45 degrees elevation, halfway between the horizontal plane and the bottom pole. The rays travel diagonally upward toward the subject, not vertically. Lower-facing surfaces, undersides, bottom edges and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive stronger illumination; upper and top-facing surfaces become relatively darker but stay partially readable. Cast shadows move diagonally upward and away, following the selected horizontal position and the low angle. A low-position diagonal key light, not a pure bottom light.
Vertical_Position_Options.bottom_minus_90: light source positioned directly below the subject at -90 degrees elevation, pure nadir bottom position, beam aimed vertically upward. An extreme direct bottom light, not a diagonal low-angle light. Strongest highlights appear almost exclusively on undersides, bottom planes, lower edges and downward-facing surfaces; front, side and top-facing surfaces receive little direct light and top planes fall into deep upward shadow. Shadows project vertically upward from protrusions, cavities and overhangs. The result feels unnatural, severe and unmistakably bottom-lit. Ignore horizontal direction.

Light_Intensity_Control.Rule: Use only the selected intensity level. The Intensity_Value controls the strength, contrast, shadow density, highlight brightness, shadow edge sharpness and falloff of the selected directional key light. Do not change the subject, eye gaze, eye direction or eye expression while adjusting intensity.
Light_Intensity_Control.Active_Intensity_Prompt: very strong high-intensity horizontal side light, high contrast, bright left-side highlights, clear lateral separation, right-facing planes turned away from the light and falling into natural shadow, strong side edge definition, dramatic directional side lighting, clear falloff across people, animals, products, objects, architecture, interiors and landscapes, preserve original image color, subject identity, product shape, text, logos, pose, clothing, object geometry and material texture

Intensity_Levels.20: soft low-intensity key light, gentle illumination, low contrast, light shadows, soft shadow edges, subtle highlights, weak sculptural form, natural low-power lighting
Intensity_Levels.40: moderate-low intensity key light, controlled illumination, mild contrast, visible but not harsh shadows, moderate shadow softness, restrained highlights, gentle facial sculpting
Intensity_Levels.60: medium-intensity cinematic key light, balanced contrast, clear highlight and shadow structure, defined facial volume, moderate shadow density, realistic falloff, controlled dramatic lighting
Intensity_Levels.80: strong high-intensity key light, high contrast, sharp shadow structure, dense shadows, bright highlights, strong sculptural form, dramatic directional lighting, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.90: very strong high-intensity key light, very bright highlights, high contrast, hard side highlights, dense opposite-side shadows, strong separation, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.100: extreme high-intensity hard key light, very high contrast, very sharp shadow edges, deep black shadows, intense specular highlights, harsh falloff, powerful sculptural lighting, severe dramatic illumination

Environment_Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply the selected lighting direction and intensity to the subject, objects and surrounding environment/background according to physical surface orientation and scene geometry. The environment may receive general brightness, exposure, contrast change, natural shadow direction toward the right, left-to-right side-light consistency and subtle brightness consistency, but must not generate visible light spots, projected circles, decorative patches, glow blobs, halos, lens flares or artificial bright stains. When Switch is off, apply the lighting mainly to the main visible content while preserving the original background as much as possible. Do not change background objects, subject identity, object/product shape, text, logos, architecture, position, composition, eye gaze or scene layout. Environmental lighting must support the selected side horizontal light direction, not flatten it.
Environment_Lighting_Control.Environment_Prompt: extend the strong horizontal side light into the surrounding environment only through realistic overall illumination, natural shadow direction, general exposure shift and subtle brightness consistency. Make the visible content and environment share the same left-side 0-degree horizontal light direction, high intensity and strong lateral contrast, with cast shadows toward the right. Left-facing surfaces and objects receive the light directly (product sides, furniture, architecture, vehicles, foliage, terrain, props and scene surfaces); right-facing surfaces are turned away from the light and fall into natural shadow, and cast shadows extend away from the left-side light. Preserve original color palette, material colors, photographic texture, environmental atmosphere, background objects, subject identity, face and gaze if present, body/clothing/pose, product shape, text, logos, object geometry, architecture, landscape structure and composition. No light spots, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flare, glow blobs, artificial halos, decorative light patterns or visible lamp effects on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture or background objects; no colored spill or color tint; no object/subject/product/architecture/scene-layout change; no gaze change if eyes present; no front, top, back or rim light.

Light_Color_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply the Main_Light_Color to the selected directional key light. When Switch is off, ignore this entire Light_Color_Control block and keep the light color natural or unchanged.
Light_Color_Control.Effect_Block: ignored because Light_Color_Control is off; no color gel lighting, no artificial colored light, no warm yellow overlay, no red tint, no blue tint, preserve natural or original light color
